gloss: the space between; distinguish, discern, understand
summary: בינ is what lies between two things and the act of telling them apart. Its commonest word, בַּיִן (construct בֵּין), is “between”: God divided between the light and the darkness (Gen 1:4), the priests were to separate between holy and common, unclean and clean (Lev 10:10), and the passover was killed בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם, “between the two evenings” (Lev 23:5). The verb בִּין is to discern, to perceive what sets one thing apart from another and so to understand, as Solomon asked “to discern between good and evil” (1Ki 3:9); its nouns בִּינָה and תְּבוּנָה are understanding, beside wisdom and knowledge. Arabic bayna “between” and bāna “be separate, distinct, plain”, and Ugaritic bn “between” beside b-y-n “understand”, show the same one root.

words.summary: A noun “interval” in form, used almost always in the construct בֵּין and with suffixes (בֵּינִי, בֵּינֵיכֶם) as the preposition “between”, often repeated before each side (“between X and between Y”). The plural בֵּינוֹת is “between, among”, and the dual בֵּנַיִם is the open ground between two armies.

senses.definition: In the space that separates two things or places, or in the middle of a pair, such as two eyes, two arms or two feet.

evidence.note: A firmament in the midst of the waters, dividing between waters and waters.
Deborah sat under the palm tree between Ramah and Bethel.
Jehu struck Jehoram between his arms.
The words bound as frontlets between your eyes.
The place of his tent at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai.
Camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea.
They passed between the parts of the calf they had cut in two.
The afterbirth that comes out from between her feet.
Yahweh speaks from between the two cherubim on the ark.

senses.gloss: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife
senses.definition: Of what joins or divides two parties: a covenant, a sign, a witness, peace, enmity or strife standing between them.

evidence.note: The sign of the covenant “between me and you and every living soul”.
“I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed.”
“My covenant between me and you and your seed after you.”
“Let there be no strife between me and you.”
Mizpah: “Yahweh watch between me and you.”
The sabbaths are a sign between Yahweh and Israel.
“Yahweh be between me and you, and between my seed and your seed, for ever.”
Yahweh has been witness between you and the wife of your youth.
“Your iniquities have separated between you and your God.”

senses.definition: With verbs of separating, distinguishing, discerning and judging: the two things set apart from each other, or the two parties a judge decides between.

evidence.note: God divided between the light and the darkness.
The priests are “to separate between the holy and between the common, and between the unclean and between the clean.”
“You will see between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not.”
לְהָבִין בֵּין־טוֹב לְרָע, “to discern between good and evil”: the verb and the preposition of this root together.
Barzillai at eighty: “Can I know between good and evil?”
Her priests have not separated between holy and common.
The priests of the house Ezekiel is shown will teach the people between holy and common.
Yahweh makes a difference between Egypt and Israel.
“Judge righteously between a man and his brother.”
“I judge between sheep and sheep.”
He will judge between the nations.
The priest values it “between good and bad”, whether good or bad.

senses.definition: Of time: chiefly בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם, “between the two evenings”, the hour of the passover and of the evening lamb, which Deuteronomy sets “at evening, at the going down of the sun”; once of an interval, “every ten days”.

evidence.note: “In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, between the two evenings, is Yahweh’s passover.”
The whole assembly kills the passover lamb between the two evenings.
The second passover, in the second month, also between the two evenings.
The daily lamb: one in the morning, the other between the two evenings.
“Between the two evenings you will eat flesh, and in the morning bread.”
Aaron burns incense when he lights the lamps between the two evenings.
וּבֵין עֲשֶׂרֶת יָמִים, once in ten days, all kinds of wine.

senses.definition: Among many: in the midst of a number of things or people. The plural בֵּינוֹת has this sense.

evidence.note: “As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.”
The lioness lay down among lions.
The cedar’s top was among the thick boughs.
A people scattered among the peoples.
בֵּינוֹת לַגַּלְגַּל, in between the wheels, and coals from between the cherubim.
The birds sing from among the branches.

senses.definition: The dual בֵּנַיִם, the ground between two drawn-up armies, in אִישׁ הַבֵּנַיִם, the man who comes out into it to fight alone: the champion.

evidence.note: Goliath goes out as אִישׁ הַבֵּנַיִם from the Philistine camp.
The setting: the Philistines on one mountain, Israel on the other, the valley between them.

greek.gloss: middle; ἀνὰ μέσον, between; ἐν μέσῳ, among

evidence.locator: בֵּין → μέσος ×296 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); 1Ki.3.9, בֵּין־ → μέσον

evidence.note: Is there not one wise man among you able to judge ἀνὰ μέσον his brother? (Deu 1:16).
The enemy sowed tares ἀνὰ μέσον the wheat.
The angels will separate the wicked ἐκ μέσου the righteous.
“There am I ἐν μέσῳ them.”

parallels.note: “In the midst of”: the firmament is בְּתוֹךְ the waters and divides בֵּין waters and waters.

phrases.gloss: between your eyes (the place of the frontlets)

evidence.note: Not to make baldness between the eyes for the dead.

phrases.gloss: the man of the space between: a champion

words.gloss: discern, perceive, understand; (hiphil) make understand, teach

senses.definition: To become aware of something through the senses, to make it out from what surrounds it: to see that something is so, to notice one among many.

evidence.note: “I saw among the simple, I discerned among the youths, a young man lacking heart.”
“He passes by me and I do not see him; he moves on and I do not perceive him.”
Eli perceived that Yahweh was calling the boy.
David saw his servants whispering and perceived that the child was dead.
“You know my sitting and my rising; you discern my thought from afar.”
Ezra viewed the people and the priests and found no sons of Levi.
Nehemiah came to Jerusalem and perceived the evil Eliashib had done.
“My eye has seen all this, my ear has heard and understood it.”

senses.definition: To turn the mind to something and weigh it.

evidence.note: “Remember the days of old, consider the years of generation and generation.”
Sitting to eat with a ruler, “consider diligently what is before you” (בִּין תָּבִין).
“If they were wise … they would consider their latter end.”
“Give ear to my words, Yahweh; consider my meditation.”
They do not regard the works of Yahweh.
The prudent considers his step.
He will not regard the gods of his fathers.

senses.definition: To grasp the meaning of what is seen, heard or read; set beside “know” and against seeing and hearing without it.

evidence.note: “Hear indeed, but do not understand; see indeed, but do not know.”
Lest they “understand with their heart, and turn, and be healed”.
“I heard, but I did not understand.”
They read in the law distinctly and gave the sense, and the people understood the reading.
Daniel understood from the books the number of the years of Jeremiah’s word.
“Understand the matter, and consider the vision.”
“None of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand.”
“That you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he.”
Man in honour who does not understand is like the beasts that perish.
Evil men do not understand judgment; those who seek Yahweh understand all.
“Who can understand his errors?”

stems.gloss: be discerning, have understanding (participle: the discerning)

senses.definition: Almost always the participle נָבוֹן, one who has understanding, set beside “wise”: a man fit to rule or judge; with a noun, skilled in something.

evidence.note: “Let Pharaoh look for a man discerning and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.”
“Take wise and understanding and known men … and I will make them heads over you.”
Keeping the statutes, Israel will be called “a wise and understanding people”.
Yahweh gives Solomon “a wise and discerning heart”.
David, נְבוֹן דָּבָר, discerning in speech.
נְבוֹן לָחַשׁ, skilled in charms.
The understanding of its understanding men will be hidden.
Woe to those wise in their own eyes and discerning in their own sight.
The king of Assyria: “by my wisdom, for I am discerning”.
“They are foolish children, and have no understanding; wise to do evil.”
The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge.
Nor riches to men of understanding, but time and chance happen to all.

senses.definition: To tell apart, to see what distinguishes right from wrong or one case from another; above all, the judge’s discerning.

evidence.note: “Give your servant a hearing heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil.”
“You asked for yourself understanding to discern judgment.”
“To discern the words of understanding.”
The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way.
“Do not be like the horse or the mule, which have no understanding.”

senses.definition: As the qal: to perceive and understand, especially visions and words; of God, to understand and regard all that men do and think.

evidence.note: God gave the four youths knowledge and skill, “and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams”.
“I was astonished at the vision, and none understood it.”
Yahweh searches all hearts and understands every imagination of the thoughts.
He fashions their hearts alike and considers all their works.
God understands the way to wisdom, and knows its place.
All who could hear with understanding.
“Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?”
They do not understand Yahweh’s counsel.
They rejoiced, because they had understood the words.

senses.definition: To cause another to understand: to explain, instruct, give understanding; the participle מֵבִין is a teacher or one skilled.

evidence.note: The Levites caused the people to understand the law.
“Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.”
“Give me understanding, and I will keep your law.”
“Your hands made me and fashioned me; give me understanding.”
The opening of your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.
Gabriel made Daniel understand.
“Whom will he make to understand the message?”
“With whom did he take counsel, and who made him understand?”
The breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
מֵבִין עִם־תַּלְמִיד, teacher as well as pupil.
Chenaniah instructed in the song, because he was skilled.
The Levites who taught all Israel.

stems.gloss: look closely, consider attentively; come to understand

senses.definition: To fix one’s eyes or mind on something and examine it.

evidence.note: “When I looked closely at him in the morning, he was not my son.”
“I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I gaze on a virgin?”
Those who see you will stare at you and consider you.
“You will look carefully at his place, and he will not be there.”
“Stand still and consider the wonders of God.”
“Send to Kedar and consider diligently.”
The wise will consider Yahweh’s lovingkindnesses.
God sees iniquity; will he not consider it?

senses.definition: To gain understanding by attending, or to understand at last what was not grasped before.

evidence.note: “The ox knows its owner … Israel does not know, my people does not understand.”
“In the latter days you will understand it perfectly” (תִּתְבּוֹנְנוּ בָהּ בִּינָה).
Kings will see what they had not been told, and understand what they had not heard.
“I understand more than the elders, because I keep your precepts.”
“Through your precepts I get understanding.”
“The thunder of his power, who can understand?”

senses.definition: Once, of Yahweh with Israel in the wilderness: to give close heed to him, watching over him; whether “instruct” is meant the verse does not settle.

evidence.note: “He found him in a desert land … he surrounded him, he attended to him (יְבוֹנְנֵהוּ), he kept him as the apple of his eye.”

evidence.locator: בִּין → συνίημι ×23 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Isa.6.9, תָּבִינוּ → συνῆτε; Isa.6.10, יָבִין → συνῶσιν; Isa.52.15, הִתְבּוֹנָנוּ → συνήσουσιν

evidence.note: Jesus quotes Isa 6:9: “hearing you will hear and not understand.”
Paul quotes Isa 6:9–10 to the Jews at Rome.
Paul quotes Isa 52:15: “those who have not heard will understand.”
The good ground is the one who hears the word and understands it.
He opened their mind to understand the scriptures.
Paul quotes Isa 29:14: “I will set aside the understanding of the συνετῶν”, for בִּינַת נְבֹנָיו.
Hidden from the wise and συνετῶν, revealed to babes.

parallels.note: “Know” and “understand” go together, and their lack together.
Seeing, with or without understanding what is seen.
Hearing, with or without understanding what is heard.
The participle נָבוֹן is paired with “wise”.

senses.definition: The power of telling right from wrong and seeing into things, set with wisdom and knowledge; it shows in patience and restraint, and Yahweh gives it.

evidence.note: “Yahweh gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.”
“Happy is the man who finds wisdom, and the man who gets understanding.”
“He who is slow to anger is of great understanding,” against the hasty who exalts folly.
A man of understanding is of a cool spirit.
A man of understanding holds his peace.
Counsel in the heart is deep water, but a man of understanding draws it out.
There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel against Yahweh.
A prince lacking understanding is a great oppressor.
A nation void of counsel, with no understanding in them.
Yahweh destroys the wise out of Edom and understanding out of the mount of Esau.
With the aged is wisdom, and in length of days understanding.
God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding.

senses.definition: The understanding by which Yahweh made and ordered the heavens and the earth, which has no limit and no one taught him.

evidence.note: “Yahweh by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens.”
He stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
“To him who made the heavens by understanding.”
By his understanding he smites through Rahab.
“There is no searching of his understanding.”
His understanding is without number.
Who showed him the way of understanding?

senses.definition: Understanding in the hands: the craftsman’s skill to devise and make, given by God for the work of the tabernacle and temple, and the idol-makers’ skill turned to idols.

evidence.note: Bezalel filled with the spirit of God in wisdom, understanding and knowledge, and all workmanship.
Hiram filled with wisdom, understanding and skill to do all work in bronze.
David guided them by the skilfulness of his hands.
Molten images “according to their own understanding”, all the work of craftsmen.
The prince of Tyre got riches by his wisdom and understanding.

evidence.locator: תְּבוּנָה → σύνεσις ×12 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Exo.31.3, תְבוּנָה → συνέσεως

evidence.note: Filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual σύνεσις.
All who heard the boy Jesus were amazed at his σύνεσις.

evidence.locator: תְּבוּנָה → φρόνησις ×7 (forms φρόνησιν, φρόνησις, φρονήσεως; MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: To turn the disobedient to the φρόνησις of the righteous.

parallels.note: Wisdom and understanding, in God’s making of the world and in man.
Knowledge and understanding from Yahweh’s mouth.

opposites.note: Folly is the opposite of understanding.

senses.definition: The power to discern and understand, beside wisdom and knowledge; to be sought and acquired, given by God, and summed up as turning from evil.

evidence.note: “The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.”
“The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.”
“Get wisdom, and with all your getting get understanding.”
To get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver.
Buy the truth, and do not sell it; wisdom, instruction and understanding.
“Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.”
Wisdom says, “I am understanding.”
Call understanding your kinswoman.
Keeping the statutes is Israel’s wisdom and understanding before the peoples.
The spirit of Yahweh on the shoot of Jesse: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding”.
The understanding of its prudent men will be hidden.
“It is a people of no understanding (בִּינוֹת); therefore he who made them will not have mercy on them.”
“Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.”
God has not given the ostrich a share in understanding.
“I have not the understanding of a man.”
David asks that Yahweh give Solomon wisdom and understanding.

senses.gloss: insight into a vision or the times
senses.definition: The understanding of what a vision, a word or the times mean, sought from God and given by him.

evidence.note: Daniel saw the vision “and sought understanding”.
“I have now come out to give you skill and understanding.”
He understood the word, and had understanding of the vision.
The sons of Issachar, “who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do”.
“In the latter days you will understand it with understanding.”
In matters of wisdom and understanding they were ten times better than all the magicians.

evidence.locator: Isa.11.2, בִינָה → συνέσεως; σύνεσις renders בִּינָה ×9 (MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: Paul quotes Isa 29:14: “I will set aside the σύνεσιν of the understanding.”
All the riches of the full assurance of σύνεσις, to know the mystery of God.
“The Lord give you σύνεσιν in all things.”

parallels.note: Wisdom and understanding are named together throughout.
“The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.”

evidence.note: In Aramaic, the same phrase.

words.summary: A word of the Persian period, used of the citadel of Susa, the fortress by the temple in Jerusalem, and once of the temple as Yahweh’s palace. It answers to Aramaic בִּירְתָא and Akkadian birtu “fort”, from which it was most probably borrowed through Aramaic; whether it goes back to the root of “between” is not clear, and it is kept here because the text’s spelling files it with בינ.

senses.definition: The fortified royal quarter of a city, as Susa the citadel, where the king held court.

evidence.note: Ahasuerus sat on his royal throne “in Susa the citadel”.

senses.definition: The fortress belonging to the house of God in Jerusalem, with its gates and its commander.

evidence.note: Timber “for the gates of the citadel which belongs to the house”.
Hananiah, ruler of the citadel.

senses.definition: The temple Solomon is to build, called a palace because it is the house of the king, Yahweh.

evidence.note: “The work is great, for the palace is not for man but for Yahweh God.”

evidence.locator: Est.1.2, בִּירָה → πόλει; πόλις renders בִּירָה ×8 (MACULA alignment)

words.summary: Once, in the plural, of Jehoshaphat’s fortresses; formed from בִּירָה, and like it most probably from Akkadian birtu through Aramaic.

senses.definition: A fortified place built to hold a land.

evidence.note: Jehoshaphat built in Judah fortresses and store cities.

senses.definition: In the space between, and with a suffix, among: as the Hebrew.

evidence.note: The bear had three ribs in its mouth “between its teeth”.
Another little horn came up “among them” (בֵּינֵיהֵן).

senses.definition: Understanding, which God gives with wisdom and knowledge.

words.summary: Emphatic בִּירְתָא; the Aramaic of Hebrew בִּירָה, most probably from Akkadian birtu.

senses.definition: A royal fortress where records were kept.

evidence.note: Cyrus’s decree was found in a scroll “at Achmetha, in the citadel in the province of Media”.

senses.definition: Between two places or parties, and between one person and another.

evidence.note: Zacharias, whom you killed “between the temple and the altar”.
“Between us and you a great gulf is fixed.”
Rebuke your brother between you and him alone.
God put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

words.gloss: among, in the midst of; (contracted בֵּית) between
words.summary: Contracted to בֵּית, which the Peshitta uses for “between” (1Co 6:5) and in Revelation for the place “between the eyes” where Greek has the forehead.

senses.definition: In the midst of a group.

evidence.note: “Where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them.”
“I am among you as one who serves.”
The enemy sowed tares among the wheat.
“Come out from among them and be separate.”
“There stands one among you whom you do not know.”

senses.definition: The contracted form, between two persons, and of the place between the eyes.

evidence.note: Is there not one wise man among you able to judge between brother and brother?
The beast’s mark is given on the right hand or “on between their eyes” (Greek: forehead).
God’s servants sealed between their eyes.
The 144,000 with the Father’s name written between their eyes.

cognates.note: Lane’s sources give بَيْنٌ as both “separation, disunion” and “distance, the space or interval between two things”, and its accusative بَيْنَ as the preposition “between” (بَيْنَ بَيْنَ, between good and bad, middling). This is Hebrew בַּיִן/בֵּין in form and sense, a noun of interval used as the preposition.

evidence.note: A separation or division between two things or lands.

cognates.gloss: be separated, distinct, plain; make distinct, explain; examine until one knows clearly
cognates.note: Form I “it became separated, severed”; form II “he made it distinct, as though separate from others; apparent, manifest, clear”; and تَبَيَّنَ, اِسْتَبَانَ “he knew it clearly, distinguished it; sought to know it, examined, scrutinized, and was not hasty”. بَيِّنٌ is “distinct, clear”, بَيِّنَةٌ “clear proof, evidence”. The Arabic runs from separating, to being distinct, to seeing distinctly and knowing: the same path as Hebrew בִּין, whose discerning is seeing “between” good and evil (1Ki 3:9).
The preposition, “between the eyes” (KTU 1.2 IV 22) and “between, among the eagles” (KTU 1.18 IV 21), from *bayn.
The verb b-y-n “understand” in Baal’s message to Anat, “I understand the lightning which the heavens do not know” (KTU 1.3 III 26–27). Ugaritic has both the preposition and the verb, as Hebrew does.

evidence.locator: p. 181, §93 Glossary, b-y-n: abn, tbn 1.3:III:26, 27 “to understand”

cognates.gloss: between; region between, interior chamber; openly; (verb) be separated, cease
cognates.note: Sabaean byn (also bn) “between”, with the noun byn “interior chamber; region between, surroundings” and bynn “openly, publicly”; the verb byn is “be dislocated, cease”, from “be separated”.

evidence.locator: p. 40, BYN I (verb); p. 41, BYN II (preposition, noun, adverb)

cognates.note: Ge’ez has the preposition bayna “between” and the verb bayyana “discern”, again both senses of the one root.

evidence.locator: SEM000685 bayn [between], GEZ001256 bayna [between] P; SEM000684 byn [separate], GEZ001255 bayyana [discern] V

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, usually plural בֵּינֵי, in the Targum of Gen 1:6 for the firmament dividing between the waters, and “wherein do they differ?” (מאי בינייהו) in the Talmud.

evidence.note: Targ. Gen. I, 6; Ḥull. 114ᵃ; Sabb. 132ᵇ.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, the pael “to teach, make wise” in the Targum of Ps 119:27 and Job 32:8, for the Hebrew hiphil “make understand”.

evidence.note: Pa. Targ. Ps. CXIX, 27; Targ. Job XXXII, 8–9.

cognates.note: Akkadian birīt “between” and the noun birītu “space between, middle part” answer to בַּיִן in sense; whether r here stands for an older y-n is not settled, so it is recorded as possible.

Akkadian birtu “fort, fortifications”, common in Assyrian records, is the source of Aramaic בִּירְתָא and of Hebrew בִּירָה, which appears only in books of the Persian period. Its tie, if any, to the root of “between” is not known.

doctrine.statement: The first works of creation are acts of dividing “between”: light and darkness, the waters above and below, day and night (Gen 1:4, 6–7, 14, 18). The priests were given the same work: “to separate between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean”, and to teach Israel to do it (Lev 10:10–11; 11:47). Ezekiel charges Jerusalem’s priests with failing to separate between holy and common (Ezk 22:26), and the priests of the house he is shown will teach the people the difference again (Ezk 44:23); Malachi says the day is coming when Israel will again “see between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not” (Mal 3:18). Solomon asked for a heart “to discern (לְהָבִין) between good and evil”, and Yahweh gave him a discerning heart (1Ki 3:9–12). Hebrews calls the mature those whose senses are trained by use “to discern both good and evil” (Heb 5:14), and Paul tells the believers to come out from among the unclean and be separate (2Co 6:17). From the verses: to understand, in this root, is first to see the difference between things that God has set apart, and the people of God are to learn to make that difference in their own lives.

Isaiah was sent to say, “Hear indeed, but do not understand; see indeed, but do not know”, lest the people “understand with their heart, and turn, and be healed” (Isa 6:9–10). Israel is worse than the ox and the ass, which know their master: “my people does not understand” (Isa 1:3). Jesus applies Isaiah’s words to those who heard his parables and did not understand (Mat 13:13–15; Mrk 4:12), and Paul to the Jews at Rome who would not believe (Act 28:25–27); the good ground is the one who “hears the word and understands it” and bears fruit (Mat 13:19, 23). Against this Isaiah foretells that kings will understand what they had not heard (Isa 52:15), which Paul applies to his preaching among the nations (Rom 15:21). The psalmist asks, “Give me understanding, and I will keep your law” (Psa 119:34), and the risen Jesus “opened their mind to understand the scriptures” (Luk 24:45). From the verses: understanding in scripture is not hearing the words but taking in their meaning with the heart so as to turn; it is lost by refusing what is heard, and given by God to those who ask for it in order to keep his word.

“Yahweh gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding” (Pro 2:6); “the fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding” (Pro 9:10), and “to depart from evil is understanding” (Job 28:28). It is God who gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge “to those who know understanding” (Dan 2:21), and it is “the breath of the Almighty” that gives men understanding (Job 32:8); the believer is not to lean on his own (Pro 3:5). Of the shoot from the stem of Jesse Isaiah says that the spirit of Yahweh will rest on him, “the spirit of wisdom and understanding” (Isa 11:1–2), and Luke records that all who heard the boy Jesus were amazed at his understanding (Luk 2:47), and that he grew in wisdom (Luk 2:52); Paul speaks of the full assurance of understanding to know the mystery of God, Christ, in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden (Col 2:2–3). From the verses: understanding is moral before it is intellectual, it is God’s gift through his word and spirit, and it rested in full on his Son.

“Yahweh by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens” (Pro 3:19); he “stretched out the heavens by his understanding” (Jer 10:12; 51:15) and “made the heavens by understanding” (Psa 136:5). Job is asked, “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding” (Job 38:4). Isaiah asks who taught Yahweh and “made him understand”, and answers that “there is no searching of his understanding” (Isa 40:14, 28); Paul quotes Isaiah’s question and adds, “O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God” (Rom 11:33–34). In Genesis the days of creation are days of dividing “between” light and darkness and the waters (Gen 1:4–7). From the verses: the heavens and the earth are the work of a mind that discerns and orders, made by Yahweh’s word in the days Genesis records, and no man was there to understand or advise it.

The passover lamb was killed on the fourteenth of the first month “between the two evenings” (Exo 12:6; Lev 23:5; Num 9:3), “at evening, at the going down of the sun, at the time you came out of Egypt” (Deu 16:6); the second lamb of the daily offering was also offered “between the two evenings” (Exo 29:39, 41; Num 28:4). Daniel was visited “about the time of the evening offering” (Dan 9:21), and the apostles went up to the temple “at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour” (Act 3:1). Jesus cried out and gave up his spirit at the ninth hour (Mat 27:46, 50; Mrk 15:34, 37), and Paul writes, “Christ our passover is sacrificed for us” (1Co 5:7). From the verses: the time of day fixed for the passover and the evening lamb is the time at which the Lamb of God died.

Israel was to bind Yahweh’s words “as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes” (Deu 6:6–8; 11:18), and the law of the firstborn and the unleavened bread was “a memorial between your eyes, that Yahweh’s law may be in your mouth” (Exo 13:9, 16). In Revelation the beast causes all to receive a mark on the right hand or, as the Peshitta words it, “between their eyes” (Rev 13:16), while God’s servants are sealed and bear the Lamb’s and the Father’s name in the same place (Rev 7:3; 14:1; 22:4). From the verses: the hand is what a man does and the place between the eyes is what governs his thinking; the law put God’s word there, and Revelation sets two claims to that place against each other, the beast’s and God’s.

Daniel “understood from the books” the seventy years of Jeremiah (Dan 9:2), and was told, “understand the matter and consider the vision” of the seventy weeks, which ends in the desolation of the city and the holy place (Dan 9:23–27). Of his last vision he says, “I heard, but I did not understand”, and is told that the words are sealed until the time of the end, when “none of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand” (Dan 12:8–10). Jeremiah twice says of Yahweh’s judgment, “in the latter days you will understand it” (Jer 23:20; 30:24). Jesus, speaking of “the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet”, says, “let him who reads understand”, and tells his disciples to flee when they see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, for “this generation will not pass away” until all is fulfilled (Mat 24:15–16, 34; Luk 21:20). From the verses: Daniel’s visions were given to be understood when their time came, and Jesus told the generation that heard him to understand and act on Daniel’s words concerning Jerusalem’s desolation, which came on that generation.
